Assessment anchored in Beige Book and SLOOS:
- Policy stance: The FOMC kept rates at 0–0.25% and reaffirmed asset purchases, repos, and reinvestments to support market functioning and credit transmission—clearly dovish with strong backstops.
- Beige Book corroboration of weak real-side conditions: Districts reported broad declines in economic activity tied to COVID-19; consumer spending fell amid retail shutdowns; construction activity contracted; agriculture deteriorated due to meat-processing plant disruptions; and employee health concerns persisted. Labor markets weakened across districts, with only selective wage increases for essential/high-demand roles while wages were flat or declining elsewhere. Pricing pressures were muted, with weaker demand and lower oil further suppressing inflation.
- Bank-lending channel (SLOOS): Banks tightened standards and terms across C&I and CRE; widened spreads; raised credit line costs; and focused on existing clients. Demand weakened in CRE and construction/land development; HELOC demand was largely unchanged but standards tightened. A relative bright spot remained government-backed mortgages.
- Net: While financial market functioning improved with Fed support, Beige Book and SLOOS indicate ongoing, material headwinds to activity, employment, and inflation. This tilts the near-term outlook more negative than market conditions alone would suggest.
